raw_case_text:
A 60-year-old patient who had attempted suicide was referred to the emergency department due to a low level of consciousness with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 11. The patient's history revealed that she had been a known case of bipolar disorder, hyperlipidemia, osteoporosis, renal stone, and water pipe smoker. The scar of an electrical burning on her right hand showed that she had a history of suicidal behavior. The patient was admitted to an intensive care unit with dizziness and drowsiness due to drug poisoning. The analysis of the patient's urine demonstrated the presence of amphetamine and benzodiazepine. On the second day of admission, the Glasgow Coma Scale score decreased to nine and then completely fell to three. The cardiac analysis findings showed the right bundle branch block and complete bundle branch block resulted from amphetamine overdose. For the elimination of amphetamine from blood circulation, several rounds of therapeutic hemodialysis had been performed. On the third day of admission, severe abdominal distension, lack of defecation, and the absence of bowel sound had occurred. The first abdominal-pelvic sonography showed a multiloculated fluid collection in the abdominal-pelvic cavity, which suggested the GI perforation and severe peritonitis. Immediately, the patient was transferred to the operation room, and laparotomy confirmed the perforation of the stomach and acute peritonitis. During the surgery, the bowel adhesion and stomach perforation were repaired. Besides, retro-gastric and sub-diaphragmatic fluid collection along with generalized peritonitis were removed by drainage. A gall bladder specimen's pathological analysis showed severe acute or chronic acalculous cholecystitis with focal mucosal necrosis.
Passing 2 weeks after the first surgery, the patient experienced severe constipation, abdominal distention, ascites, and edema. The second abdominal-pelvic sonography revealed the multicoated fluid collection and septation in the abdominal-pelvic cavity, which necessitated the second laparotomy. After the second surgery, sepsis disseminated intravascular coagulation and the increase in serum BUN and creatinine levels, resulting in renal failure, occurred. Finally, cardiorespiratory arrest led to patient death related to multidrug poisoning (alprazolam and amphetamine), metabolic encephalopathy, perforation of peptic ulcers, and sepsis. The pathology report of partial gastrectomy revealed gastric perforation with severe CMV gastritis, ulceration, and foreign body-type giant cell reaction. Immunohistochemistry staining using a monoclonal antibody against CMV pp65 antigen indicated CMV immunoreactivity with brownish areas (shown in Fig. 1). A nested-PCR confirmed CMV infection for CMV DNA in gall bladder specimens and gastric wall biopsy (shown in Fig. 2).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 60-year-old female presented to the emergency department with depressed consciousness (GCS 11), dizziness, and drowsiness following an intentional multidrug overdose, progressing on hospital day 3 to severe abdominal distension, obstipation, and acute peritonitis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Admitted to the ICU after a suicide attempt with multidrug ingestion (amphetamine and alprazolam), the patient deteriorated on hospital day 2 with right/complete bundle branch block and deep coma (GCS 9 dropping to 3, treated with hemodialysis), and on hospital day 3 developed severe abdominal distension, obstipation, and absent bowel sounds from a perforated stomach requiring emergency laparotomy, gastric perforation repair, adhesiolysis, and cholecystectomy. Two weeks postoperatively, recurrent abdominal distension, constipation, ascites, and multiloculated intra-abdominal collections necessitated a second laparotomy and partial gastrectomy, complicated postoperatively by sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and acute renal failure.
subjective.past_medical_history: Bipolar disorder, prior suicide attempt (resulting in an old electrical burn scar on the right hand), hyperlipidemia, osteoporosis, nephrolithiasis, and water-pipe smoking.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for dizziness, drowsiness, coma, severe abdominal distension, and obstipation.

objective.physical_examination: On admission: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score 11/15 (declining to 9 and 3 on day 2) and an old electrical burn scar on the right hand. On hospital day 3: severe abdominal distension and absent bowel sounds.
objective.routine_investigations: Urine toxicology screen was positive for amphetamine and benzodiazepines. Cardiac/ECG monitoring showed right bundle branch block and complete bundle branch block. Post-second-laparotomy labs showed elevated BUN and creatinine (acute kidney injury) and coagulopathy consistent with DIC. Abdominopelvic ultrasounds on hospital day 3 and at 2 weeks post-op demonstrated multiloculated septated intra-abdominal fluid collections.
objective.advanced_workup: Emergency laparotomies (day 3 and week 2) revealed gastric perforation and generalized peritonitis. Gallbladder histopathology showed severe acute and chronic acalculous cholecystitis with focal mucosal necrosis. Partial gastrectomy histopathology demonstrated gastric perforation with severe ulcerative cytomegalovirus (CMV) gastritis and foreign-body giant cell reaction, confirmed by positive anti-CMV pp65 monoclonal antibody immunohistochemistry and positive nested PCR for CMV DNA in both the gastric wall and gallbladder specimens.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Fatal ulcerative cytomegalovirus (CMV) gastritis complicated by gastric perforation and CMV acalculous cholecystitis following intentional amphetamine and alprazolam poisoning, confirmed by partial gastrectomy histopathology, positive anti-CMV pp65 immunohistochemistry, and positive nested PCR for CMV DNA in both gastric and gallbladder tissues. Despite hemodialysis and two emergency laparotomies with gastric resection and cholecystectomy, the patient died postoperatively from sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, acute renal failure, and cardiorespiratory arrest.
